title: Word Order

explanation.en: English statements commonly use subject–verb–object order. Time expressions often come at the end.
explanation.taglish: Common sa English ang subject–verb–object. Madalas nasa dulo ang time expression. Halimbawa: I check my email every morning.
explanation.fil: Karaniwang ayos ng pahayag sa English ang simuno, pandiwa, at layon. Maaaring ilagay sa dulo ang oras.

examples: I check my email every morning.

exercises.prompt: Choose the usual subject–verb–object order for a neutral statement.
exercises.explanation: The usual order for a neutral statement is subject + verb + object: I + review + the plan.

exercises.prompt: Which word is the verb: 'They prepare dinner'?
exercises.explanation: 'Prepare' is the action, so it is the verb. 'They' is the subject and 'dinner' is the object.
Put the subject 'He' before the verb 'sends', then the object 'the email'.
'We meet on Monday' uses subject + verb + time. You can also say 'On Monday, we meet.'
exercises.hint: Place the day after the action.

exercises.explanation: 'My colleague' is the subject, 'reviews' is the verb, and 'the figures' is the object.
exercises.hint: Find who, what they do, and what they review.

writing.prompt: Write a sentence about something you do each morning.
checklist: I put the subject before the verb.
I placed the object after the verb, if needed.
I placed the time expression clearly.
writing.exampleAnswer: I review the schedule every morning.

optionalSpeaking.prompt: Describe your morning routine in two or three sentences. Use subject + verb, and add a time expression.

sections.heading: Basic order
sections.explanation: Start with the subject, then the verb, then the object when there is one.

sections.heading: Adding time
sections.explanation: Time words often go at the end of a sentence.
sections.example: I review the report every Monday.

sections.heading: Questions are different
sections.explanation: Questions may change the word order.
sections.example: Do you review the report every Monday?

guidedSteps: Start with the person or thing doing the action.
Put the action after the subject.
Add what receives the action and when it happens.
commonMistake: For a clear neutral statement, say 'I check my email every morning.' A time phrase can also come first: 'Every morning, I check my email.'
